Methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate (methyl lactate) contains a chiral carbon (with –H, –OH, –CH₃, –COOCH₃) and thus exhibits optical isomerism. Dimethyl fumarate is a trans-alkene with identical substituents, making it achiral (it has a center of symmetry) and incapable of optical isomerism. Therefore, methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate shows optical isomerism.

Optical isomerism occurs when a molecule is chiral (has no plane of symmetry, no center of inversion, etc.) and exists as non-superimposable mirror images. Typically, molecules with a chiral carbon (carbon with four different substituents) show optical isomerism. Also, some molecules without chiral centers can be chiral due to axial chirality or helicity, but here we have simple molecules.

Methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate: Also known as methyl lactate. The structure: CH3-CH(OH)-COOCH3. The carbon with the OH group (carbon 2) is chiral: it has H, OH, CH3, and COOCH3. So it is a chiral molecule. It exists as R and S enantiomers. So it shows optical isomerism.
